routing_warnings.description: The room-wall shift is specifically requested to narrow the common corridor, making the corridor-layout Requirement the better target.
The proposed turquoise-line wall reallocates common entrance-hall area to unit 1 and primarily changes shared-space boundaries.
Expansion to the turquoise line changes the unit 1 bathroom boundary rather than the general partition-wall layout.
The message identifies a partition wall to be constructed in the corridor and is better routed to the specific partition-wall Requirement than to shared-space geometry.
The proposed unit 3 counter position and bathroom-door clearance concern the unit-specific counter-location Requirement.
The kitchen-counter relocation clause concerns unit-specific counter placement rather than the common cabinetry specification.
The instruction to remove the purple walls also changes the partition-wall layout; only the counter-side condition and refrigerator request are retained for the target Requirement.
The proposed swap of unit 1's kitchen and common bathroom concerns their relative arrangement rather than the common cabinetry specification.
The request to show shower, sink, and door dimensions concerns the dimensioned-plan deliverable rather than changing the en-suite behavior.
The request to replace the unit 1 sliding bathroom door with a hinged door belongs to the independently defined bathroom-door operation Requirement.
The request to add bathroom-door edge dimensions concerns the dimensioned-plan deliverable.
The requested inward-opening direction and fixture clearance concern the independently defined unit 1 bathroom-door operation.
The reported sink collision and 55 cm clearance concern the unit 1 bathroom-door operation rather than the en-suite mechanism as a whole.
The request to add the en-suite wall-to-door-edge measurement belongs to the dimensioned-plan deliverable.
The freelancer's claim that the requested measurement is being added belongs to the dimensioned-plan deliverable.
This message asks how the unit 3 toilet drain can reach the existing waste connection.
This message addresses responsibility for resolving the unit 3 toilet drain during construction.
The request to move the unit 3 drain to the left wall belongs to the separate drain-routing Requirement; only the shower-location clause is retained here.
The complaint that the unit 3 bathroom width is missing concerns dimension annotation rather than a change to the bathroom geometry.
This message concerns positioning bathrooms generally relative to the two existing toilet pipes rather than the unit 3-specific routing path.
The client requests that toilet positions across the bathrooms be updated relative to existing drains; the source does not specifically identify unit 3.
This request concerns moving an unspecified toilet closer to a drain pipe and follows discussion of unit 1, so it does not entail a unit 3 routing Event.
The reported fixture-fit constraint and alternative arrangement concern the Unit 1 en-suite bathroom design rather than completion of the overall floor-plan deliverable.
This message reports fixture-fit geometry rather than confirming that dimensions were annotated on the plan.
This message reports that the proposed en-suite layout cannot fit the sink and washing machine, not a failure of the dimensioned-plan deliverable.
The clause requesting conversion of the Unit 1 sliding bathroom door to a hinged door belongs to the bathroom-door-operation Requirement.
This message specifically asks how the unit 3 toilet drain can reach the existing WC drain.
This design-responsibility conflict directly responds to the unit 3 toilet-drain routing question.
The requested drain relocation is explicitly limited to the unit 3 bathroom.
